situation:
You and your teammate are the compliance director and the marketing director at NORTHWATER DIAGNOSTICS, a clinical laboratory that runs blood work for physician offices and two hospital systems. The founder and chief executive officer (judge), who opened the laboratory nineteen years ago, is preparing to sell the business and retire within the year, and has asked the two of you to meet.

NORTHWATER is profitable, and its reputation is built on people. Couriers and phlebotomists are the only part of the company most clinics ever see, and physicians renew because results arrive when they were promised. The laboratory belongs to a regional association of independent labs whose members meet quarterly to talk through staffing shortages, courier routes, reagent supply and reimbursement trends.

At last quarter's meeting, executives from two competing member labs began urging everyone in the room to stop quoting the routine wellness panel below a stated figure. A NORTHWATER sales representative of twelve years sat through it, said nothing, and the following week sent clinics a promotional email announcing the panel's new association price. The representative has never been disciplined and does not appear to see a problem.

NORTHWATER is also days from signing for a high-throughput analyzer that would cut turnaround time roughly in half. The equipment pays for itself only if panel volume grows the way the association's shared forecast predicts, and that forecast assumes the panel holds its current price. The hospital system that sends NORTHWATER its outpatient work has already been told the faster turnaround is coming.

The founder (judge) wants the two of you to analyze what happened at the meeting, decide what NORTHWATER says to the representative and to the clinics that received the email, recommend whether the laboratory signs for the analyzer now, and propose rules governing how staff take part in association business. Waiting until NORTHWATER can verify demand on its own delays the equipment and may cost the hospital contract; signing now commits the laboratory to payments a softer market may not cover.

You will present your recommendation to the founder (judge) in the founder's office at the laboratory. The founder (judge) will greet the two of you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the founder's questions, the founder (judge) will thank you for your work.
